keyFindings.description: Regression lock missing: the `verdict !== "died"` guard (no worker-queued for the terminal failure) and the spec's 'spawn_worker still answers queued' rule are exercised by no test — both LEGION-93 tests reach the terminal crossing through the drain. Code verified correct by reading. Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071247

Wording: the /worker/ready row's 'third failure at ready ... worker-died' clause is unreachable (freshClaim starts promptFailures fresh; a ready-time prompt is always the pane's first failure). Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071254

Wording: 'Both counters are cleared only by a started turn' contradicts the same bullet (promptFailures returns to zero at each retirement and restarts on the relaunched claim); only promptRetires is cleared solely by a started turn. Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071260

Wording: 'acknowledged every prompt' is narrower than the code — a refused prompt counts in the same promptFailures (LEGION-60), so a persistently refusing worker reaches the same verdict; same narrowing in the promptRetires doc comment (legion-state.ts:152-154). Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071263

No action: markWorkerDeadLocked persists before removeFromQueue and the counter writes, so a crash in that millisecond window relaunches once more before the bound — one extra cycle, never unbounded; the ordering is the spec's StopFailed choice. Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071266

Test hygiene: toHaveLength(4) pins console.error volume; promptFailures/launchFailures toBeUndefined() pin field absence rather than behaviour; the 50-tick onceEventLoop budget is the load-sensitive race the fixture's comment rejects. Thread https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/pull/1082#discussion_r4003071269
